name: Titanium.UI.Tab
description:
A `TabGroup` tab instance. Each tab includes a button and one or more windows, which
holds the "contents" of the tab. Users can select a tab by clicking on the tab button.

Use the [Titanium.UI.createTab](api:Titanium.UI#createTab) method or **`<Tab>`** Alloy element to create a tab.

Use [TabGroup.setActiveTab](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup#setActiveTab) to switch between tabs
in a tab group.

The behavior of tabs and tab groups follows the platform's native navigation style,
which varies significantly between platforms.

#### iOS Platform Implementation Notes

On iOS, the tab maintains a stack of windows. Windows on top
of the stack can partially or totally obscure windows lower in the stack.  Calling
[open](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#open) opens a new window on top of the window stack. When a window
is closed, either by the user or by code, the window is removed from the stack, making
the previous window visible. The root tab window cannot be removed.

On iOS the tab controls are generally kept on screen to allow a user to
navigate inside the app. Tab controls are hidden when the user is performing a modal
task (for example, composing a message). In this case, the app should provide a button
in the navigation bar to return to the previous screen. On iOS, the window should also
be opened as modal. On iOS, The tab controls can also be hidden by opening the new window
with [tabBarHidden](api:Titanium.UI.Window#tabBarHidden) set to `true`.

When closing a tab window in iOS, you should always use the
[Tab.close](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#close) method to ensure that the tab group maintains its
navigation state.

#### Android Platform Implementation Notes

On Android, the tab does not maintain a stack of windows.
Calling [open](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#open) opens a new, heavyweight window, which
by default covers the tab group entirely. This seems quite different from the iOS model,
but it is the standard model for Android applications. Users can use the **Back** button
to close the window and return to the tab group.

On Android, tab windows can be closed using either
[Tab.close](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#close) or [Window.close](api:Titanium.UI.Window#close). Since
no window stack is maintained, only a single window opened using
[Tab.open](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#open) can be closed using `Tab.close`.

As on iOS, the root tab window cannot be closed.

examples.title: Simple Tab Example
Alloy XML Markup
examples.code:
Previous example an an Alloy view.

``` xml
<Alloy>
    <TabGroup id="tabGroup">
        <Tab id="tab" title="My Tab" icon="myicon.png">
            <Window id="window" title="My Tab" />
        </Tab>
      </TabGroup>
</Alloy>
```

properties.name: active
properties.summary: `true` if this tab is active, `false` if it is not.
properties.description:
The tab can be activated by setting the property, but since this property is
platform-specific, using [TabGroup.setActiveTab](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup#setActiveTab)
is recommended instead.

properties.name: activeIcon
properties.summary: Icon URL for this tab when active.
properties.description:
If unspecified, iOS uses a tint color to indicate the active tab. See
[icon](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#icon) for more information.

If the icon provided is larger than [30 pixels (60 pixels for retina, 90 pixels for super-retina)]
(https://developer.apple.com/ios/human-interface-guidelines/icons-and-images/image-size-and-resolution/),
this image will be scaled to fit.

properties.name: activeIconIsMask
properties.summary: Defines if the active icon property of the tab must be used as a mask.
properties.description:
This is the equivalent of the [iconIsMask](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#iconIsMask) property, but for the active icon. When this is true, the active icon is
tinted with the color specified in [tabsTintColor](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup#tabsTintColor). When this is false the image is rendered as is, though the
title of the tab is still tinted.

properties.name: activeTintColor
properties.summary: Defines the color of the tab icon when it is active.

properties.name: activeTitleColor
properties.summary: Defines the color of the title of tab when it's active.
properties.description: The color of the title of the tab when it's active.

properties.name: backgroundColor
properties.summary: Sets the color of the tab when it is inactive.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: backgroundFocusedColor
properties.summary: Sets the color of the tab when it is focused.
properties.description:
On the Android platform, this sets the color of the active tab and is only supported by
[TABS_STYLE_BOTTOM_NAVIGATION](api:Titanium.UI.Android#TABS_STYLE_BOTTOM_NAVIGATION).

For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: badge
properties.summary: Badge value for this tab. `null` indicates no badge.
properties.description:
On the Android platform you will need to use a Theme with `parent="Theme.MaterialComponents.*"`
in order to use a badge. You have to pass a number as a string. Non-numeric characters will not be displayed.

On iOS, a badge will only be shown if the tab has been assigned an icon. Text only tabs do not support badges.

properties.name: badgeBackgroundColor
properties.summary:
If this item displays a badge, this color will be used for the badge's background.
If set to null, the default background color will be used instead.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: badgeColor
properties.summary:
If this item displays a badge, this color will be used for the badge's background.
If set to null, the default background color will be used instead.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: badgeTextColor
properties.summary: Set the text color of the badge.
properties.description: For information about color values, see the "Colors" section of [Titanium.UI](api:Titanium.UI).

properties.name: icon
properties.summary: Icon URL for this tab.
properties.description:
#### iOS Tab Icons

On iOS, tab icons are usually white with a transparent background. The system uses
a transparent tint color to indicate whether the tab is active or inactive. In the
inactive state, the tint color is based on the tab bar's color
[tabsBackgroundColor](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup#tabsBackgroundColor), which defaults
to black. In the active state, the tint color is usually blue. Prior to Titanium
3.1, there was no way to override the default active icon tint.

Some icon-related features:

*   You can specify the active tab's tint color as
[activeTabIconTint](api:Titanium.UI.TabGroup#activeTabIconTint).

*   You can set separate icon images for the active and inactive states. If
[activeIcon](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#activeIcon) is set, then `icon` is used in the
inactive state, and `activeIcon` is used in the active state. **No default tint
is applied to either icon.**

 If the icon provided is larger than [30 pixels (60 pixels for retina, 90 pixels for super-retina)]
 (https://developer.apple.com/ios/human-interface-guidelines/icons-and-images/image-size-and-resolution/),
 this image will be scaled to fit if used with activeIcon, and cropped at the bottom
 otherwise.

 #### Android Tab Icons
 Can be used in combination with `iconFamily` in a BottomNavigation setup with `experimental:true`.

properties.name: iconFamily
properties.summary: Specifies the font family or specific font to use.
properties.description:
When using a BottomNavigation setup with `experimental:true` you can use this property in combination
with an `icon` to use an icon-font for the tab icons:

``` js
'#tab1': {
  icon: "\ueac1",
  iconFamily: "tabler-icons"
}
```

properties.name: iconInsets
properties.summary: The icon inset or outset for each edge.
properties.description:
Use this property for example to center an icon without providing a title. To do that, set the
insets to `{ top: 6 }` and/or `{ left: 6 }`. The `right` and `bottom` are calculated internally to prevent the
icon from mutating.

inlined.name: TabIconInsets
inlined.summary: Dictionary to specify edge insets for [Titanium.UI.Tab.iconInsets](api:Titanium.UI.Tab#iconInsets). Difference from typical [Padding](api:Padding) is that `right` and `bottom` are ignored and calculated internally from `top`/`left` values.

properties.name: left
properties.summary: Left inset.

properties.name: top
properties.summary: Top inset.

properties.name: iconIsMask
properties.summary: Defines if the icon property of the tab must be used as a mask.
properties.description:
When this property is true, the color data of the image specified as the icon is ignored and the image is used as an alpha mask.
When this is false, the color data of the image is preserved.

properties.name: tintColor
properties.summary: Defines the color of the tab icon.

properties.name: title
properties.summary: Title for this tab.

properties.name: titleColor
properties.summary: Defines the color of the title of tab when it's inactive.
properties.description: The color of the title of the tab when it's inactive.

properties.name: titleid
properties.summary: Key identifying a string from the locale file to use for the tab title. Only one of `title` or `titleid` should be specified.

properties.name: window
properties.summary: Root-level tab window.  All tabs must have at least one root-level tab window.

methods.name: close
methods.summary: Closes the top-level window for this tab.
methods.description:
On iOS, this method should be used when closing a window opened from a tab, to
correctly maintain the iOS tab group's navigation state. Note that the window to
be closed **must** be passed in as a parameter:

``` js
myTab.close(tabWin);
```

On Android, this method does **not** take a `window` parameter.

``` js
myTab.close();
```

On Android, if a window has been opened in front of the tab using `Tab.open`,
a subsequent call to `Tab.close` is equivalent to calling `close` on that window.
No window stack is maintained, so only the most-recently opened window on a given
tab can be closed in this way.

All platforms accept an optional `options` parameter. The only supported property
for this dictionary is the `animated` flag, which specifies whether the window
close should be animated. `animated` is true by default.

parameters.name: window
parameters.summary: Window to close. This parameter **must** be omitted on Android.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
Dictionary of display and animation settings to use when closing the window.
Identical to the `options` parameter to [Window.close](api:Titanium.UI.Window#close).
iOS only supports the **animated** parameter.

methods.name: open
methods.description: On iOS, the new window is opened as the top window in the tab's window stack. On Android, the new window is opened as a new, heavyweight window, obscuring the tab group.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
Dictionary of display and animation settings to use when opening the window.
Identical to the `options` parameter to [Window.open](api:Titanium.UI.Window#open).
iOS only supports the **animated** parameter.

methods.name: popToRootWindow
methods.summary: Closes all windows that are currently opened inside the tab.
methods.description: Note that only the `close` event of the most recently opened window is fired.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
iOS only: Options supporting a single `animated` boolean property to determine whether the windows
will be animated while being closed (default: false).

methods.name: setWindow
methods.summary: Sets the root window that appears in the tab.
methods.description:
You can only use this method to set the tab's root window before the TabGroup containing this tab
is opened, that is, once the TabGroup is displayed, you cannot change the root window
that appears in the tab.

deprecated.notes: Set the value of the [window](Titanium.UI.Tab.window) property directly.
